body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Dead compact handling left in the Size block**

The Size block is now rendered only when `!compact`, so `compact={compact}` on this RadioChips is always false and can be dropped. The `sizes`, `valueText` and `onSliderKey` values (lines 276-308) are also still computed on every compact render though nothing uses them there. If the CSS still has `.fields[data-compact]` rules for the slider, ticks or range, those are dead too.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in 9f1e845e: the Size chips now pass `compact={false}`. Keeping `sizes`, `valueText` and `onSliderKey` where they are. They are a few string lookups per render, and moving them into the `!compact` branch adds churn for no measurable gain. None of the `[data-compact]` CSS rules are dead: `.chips[data-compact] .chip` still styles the Shape chips, and the slider, ticks and range have no compact rules.

**Looks addressed** at `9f1e845`: The Size chips no longer pass `compact={compact}`. They pass the literal `false` (line 341), which fits because `RadioChips` declares `compact: boolean` as required (line 46). I agree with leaving `sizes`, `valueText` and `onSliderKey` where they are. The `[data-compact]` CSS is still used: `.chips[data-compact] .chip` styles the Shape chips (css line 53).

**Looks addressed** at `69fdf57`: Thanks. Passing `compact={false}` on the Size chips in 9f1e845e covers it. Your reasoning for keeping the cheap `sizes`, `valueText` and `onSliderKey` computations and the `[data-compact]` CSS rules is fine.
